---
title: "4.4 Example with 4 DV Categories"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

- Example --- GSS 1972 -- 2021
  - DV = views of premarital sex
  - Focal IVs:
    - How have views changed over time (i.e., *year*)?\*
    - How does religiosity pattern views (i.e., *religious* binary)?

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss", clear

// Data cleaning //
gen religous = attend
lab var religous "Religious Attendee"
recode religous 0/3 = 0 4/8 = 1
lab def religlab 0"Not Religious" 1"Religious"
lab val religous religlab

drop if missing(premarsx, college, age, woman, race3, year1972, religous)

fre premarsx
<</dd_do>>
```

## R

```{r}
library(haven)           # import Stata data and labels
library(dplyr)           # data manipulation
library(sjmisc)          # frq() frequency tables
library(ggplot2)         # graphs
library(nnet)            # multinomial logit: multinom()
library(marginaleffects) # predictions and marginal effects
library(cleanplots)      # graph scheme
cleanplots_defaults()

gss <- read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/cda_gss.dta")

# Data cleaning: religious attendee = attends about once a month or more
gss <- gss |>
  mutate(religous = case_when(attend <= 3 ~ 0, attend >= 4 ~ 1))

# Keep model variables; drop any missing data
gss <- gss[c("premarsx", "college", "age", "woman", "race3", "year1972", "religous")]
gss <- gss[complete.cases(gss), ]

frq(gss$premarsx)

# Treat binary/nominal variables as factors
gss <- gss |>
  mutate(across(c(premarsx, college, woman, race3), as_factor),
    religous = factor(religous, labels = c("Not Religious", "Religious")),
    year1972 = as.numeric(year1972)) |>
  droplevels()
```

:::

\**year* has a highly nonlinear relationship with this outcome. [See the Appendix](appendix-4a-combining-outcomes.qmd#nonlinear-functional-forms) for how I worked out how to specify *year* in the model

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
*Preferred model with year^3
qui mlogit premarsx c.year1972##c.year1972##c.year1972 ///
    i.religous i.college c.age i.woman i.race3
est store psmod

*4.4.b
qui margins, at(year1972=(0(1)49))
marginsplot, ylab(0(.1).7) plotop(msym(none) lwid(*1.4)) ///
    recastci(rline) ciopt(col(*.4)) ///
    xlab(0"1972" 8"1980" 18"1990" 28"2000" 38"2010" 49"2021") xtitle("GSS Survey Year") ///
    ytitle("Pr(View of Premarital Sex as Wrong)") ///
    title("[4.4.b] Predicted Probabilities of Views About When Premarital Sex is Wrong", size(*1.1)) ///
    legend(order(5 "Always" 6 "Usually" 7 "Sometimes" 8 "Not Wrong"))
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/cda-04_04_b-prems-02.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

![](fig/cda-04_04_b-prems-02.png){width=80% fig-alt="[4.4.b] Predicted probabilities of each view of premarital sex from 1972 to 2021: not wrong at all rises from about 0.30 to 0.67, always wrong falls from about 0.33 to 0.15, sometimes wrong falls from about 0.24 to 0.13, and usually wrong falls from about 0.12 to 0.05."}

## R

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "[4.4.b] Predicted probabilities of each view of premarital sex from 1972 to 2021: not wrong at all rises from about 0.30 to 0.67, always wrong falls from about 0.33 to 0.15, sometimes wrong falls from about 0.24 to 0.13, and usually wrong falls from about 0.12 to 0.05."
# Preferred model with year^3. Year is divided by 10 inside the polynomial so
# that R computes the standard errors accurately (predictions are the same)
psmod <- multinom(premarsx ~ poly(I(year1972 / 10), 3, raw = TRUE) +
  religous + college + age + woman + race3, data = gss, trace = FALSE)

# 4.4.b
plot_predictions(psmod, by = c("year1972", "group"),
  newdata = datagrid(year1972 = 0:49, grid_type = "counterfactual")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("red", "skyblue", "gray50", "black"),
    labels = c("Always", "Usually", "Sometimes", "Not Wrong")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "skyblue", "gray50", "black"),
    labels = c("Always", "Usually", "Sometimes", "Not Wrong")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 8, 18, 28, 38, 49),
    labels = c("1972", "1980", "1990", "2000", "2010", "2021")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, .7, .1), limits = c(0, .7)) +
  labs(title = "[4.4.b] Predicted Probabilities of Views About When Premarital Sex is Wrong",
    x = "GSS Survey Year", y = "Pr(View of Premarital Sex as Wrong)",
    color = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot")
```

:::

## AMEs for effect of time across range

- Yet another **amount( )** we can specify with **mecompare** is the **range** (In R, **minmax** on **avg_comparisons**)
  - This will calculate the effect of a change from the minimum to the maximum of your IV
    - Here, the total effect that time has had over the measured range of 1972 to 2021
  - Usually I recommend the **trimrange** (5^th^ to 95^th^ percentile), but **range** is OK here as there is an entire GSS sample (*n* $\approx$ 2000) at the min and max values

::: {.callout-note icon="false" appearance="simple"}
[Bonus stats tip]{.underline}: *N* refers to the whole sample (*N* = 40,486) while *n* refers to a subsample. Subscripts are often useful, e.g., *n*~2021~=2,399. Statistics like *N* and *n* are always italicized.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
*AMEs across entire range of year variable
mecompare year1972, amount(range) model(psmod)
<</dd_do>>
```

## R

```{r}
# AMEs across entire range of year variable
avg_comparisons(psmod, variables = list(year1972 = "minmax"))
```

:::

> *From 1972 to 2021, views toward premarital sex have become more accepting. The largest change in opinions of premarital sex have been in the amount of US adults saying it is "not wrong at all." Specifically, the probability of thinking premarital sex is not wrong at all has increased by about 0.36 over the last 49 years. This change has been offset by decreasing numbers of individuals stating that premarital sex is always wrong (∆ = -0.18), usually wrong (∆ = -0.07), and sometimes wrong (∆ = -0.12).*

::: {.callout-note icon="false" appearance="simple"}
[Interpretation tip:]{.underline} It is easy for readers to get lost with so many MEs. Set the scene with a non-technical takeaway summary sentence first. Then, add specific #s and details.
:::

## AMEs for effect of religiosity

- Here, "*religious*" = someone who attends religious services ≥ once a month

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
*4.4.c
est restore psmod
qui margins, dydx(religous)
marginsplot, recast(bar) ciopts(color(gs5)) ///
    xlab(0.5 " " 1 "Always" 2 "Usually" 3 "Sometimes" 4 "Not Wrong" 4.5 " ") ///
    yline(0) plotopts(barw(0.6) color(purple)) ylab(, format(%4.2f)) ///
    xtitle("View of When Premarital Sex is Wrong") ytitle("AME of Religiosity") ///
    title("[4.4.c] Average Marginal Effects of Religiosity on Views of Premarital Sex", size(*1.1)) ///
    subtitle("Effects Above Zero Indicate That View is More Likely for Someone who is Religious", size(small))
<</dd_do>>
<<dd_do: quietly>>
graph export "fig/cda-04_04_c-prems-03.png", replace width(1400)
<</dd_do>>
```

![](fig/cda-04_04_c-prems-03.png){width=80% fig-alt="[4.4.c] Bar chart of the average marginal effects of religiosity on each view of premarital sex: about 0.26 for always wrong, 0.05 for usually wrong, about 0 for sometimes wrong, and -0.30 for not wrong at all."}

## R

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "[4.4.c] Bar chart of the average marginal effects of religiosity on each view of premarital sex: about 0.26 for always wrong, 0.05 for usually wrong, about 0 for sometimes wrong, and -0.30 for not wrong at all."
# 4.4.c
me_relig <- avg_comparisons(psmod, variables = "religous")

ggplot(me_relig, aes(x = group, y = estimate)) +
  geom_col(width = .6, fill = "purple") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = .1, color = "gray30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Always", "Usually", "Sometimes", "Not Wrong")) +
  labs(title = "[4.4.c] Average Marginal Effects of Religiosity on Views of Premarital Sex",
    subtitle = "Effects Above Zero Indicate That View is More Likely for Someone who is Religious",
    x = "View of When Premarital Sex is Wrong", y = "AME of Religiosity") +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot")
```

:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Stata

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
*AMEs for binary IV
mecompare religous, model(psmod)
<</dd_do>>
```

## R

```{r}
# AMEs for binary IV
me_relig
```

:::

> *Religiosity has a polarizing effect on views of premarital sex. Religious individuals are much more likely to view premarital sex as always wrong (ME = 0.257) and somewhat more likely to view it as usually wrong (ME = 0.047). In contrast, they are much less likely to view premarital sex as not wrong at all (ME = -0.299). There are no differences in views of premarital sex as sometimes wrong based on religiosity.*

::: {.callout-note icon="false" appearance="simple"}
[Interpretation tip]{.underline}: It is common for some MEs to be significant and some null. Usually, best to explicitly note null effects on an outcome category.
:::
